thread.title: Apple’s stock makes brief intraday foray into bear-market territory

author: Stocks News Feed
title: Apple’s stock makes brief intraday foray into bear-market territory
text:
Shares of Apple Inc.
 AAPL, -3.56%
 dipped briefly into bear-market territory in intraday trade Monday before bouncing back out of it. The stock was down 3.5% in midday trade, but was down as much as 4.1% at its intraday low of $185.63, which was 20.01% below its Oct. 3 record high close of $232.07. Many chart watchers define a bear market as a decline on a closing basis of 20% or more from a bull-market high. A close at or below $185.65 would mark the first bear market for Apple’s stock in over two years. The previous bear market, which started in Aug. 21, 2015 didn’t end until Aug. 9, 2016, when the stock closed 20.44% above its May 12, 2016 bear-market closing low of $90.34. Apple had fallen to an intraday low of $185.93 last Wednesday, before bouncing. The stock accelerated to the downside last week after a number of smartphone suppliers cut revenue guidance, citing requests for reduced deliveries by a large customer. The stock was still up 10% year to date, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average
 DJIA, -1.63%
 has gained 1.1%.
